craft-libs.why: craft-web-recovery: crash-recovery copies of unsaved documents in the browser (IndexedDB, one Web Lock per tab, counted only after commit), the unload guard and download helpers; shared by every app's web save fixes, not in storytold's craft-libs yet (storytold/craft-libs#124)

patches.why: Safari's WebGPU refuses fxn_median_huang (its 2048-entry histogram is over WebKit's 8192-byte limit on a function's variables), and since every kernel shares one module the whole GPU compositor goes; the histogram now packs 16-bit counts. Also: a second tab restored the first tab's live project and overwrote its session snapshot (one slot per site); only the first tab keeps the session now, and the second says so

Since 0.17.0 the web zip ships wasm-bindgen's snippets only at the top, but app/photocraft-web.js imports ./snippets/… next to itself: inline0.js 404s and the app hangs on "Loading PhotoCraft…" (storytold/photocraft#10491, #10017)

The web build never autosaved: no recovery storage, and an idle page draws no frames so the autosave tick never ran; a reload or crashed tab lost unsaved documents (storytold/photocraft#6615). Uses craft-web-recovery from the craft-libs override.
Safari writes the whole wasm heap to OPFS when given a view into it, so crash-recovery snapshots and meta were 15 MB of garbage and nothing was recovered; the bytes are copied first

A crashed tab's recovery copies were only offered after three save intervals (its heartbeat still counted though its Web Lock was gone), copies lived in local storage (about 5 MB shared by every app on the site), and leaving with unsaved changes didn't ask; now offered at once, kept in IndexedDB, and leaving asks first
